findings.issue: The close now leaves out every PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row, including the plugin's own `.claude/audit.config.json` and `.claude/.gitignore`, whether git tracks them or not. A task that edits a TRACKED config without declaring it used to be refused by the close as an undeclared change made during the attempt. It is now named in an informational line and the close goes ahead with that edit left uncommitted. The commit step already did the same (ctw-at7 pins the config as left out), so the two readers agree, which is the point of the task. But the new lo-po cases pin only the restore point; none pins a tracked config edit, so the widening is unexamined.
findings.resolution: Keep the commit and the close in agreement, since exempting only untracked config in the close alone would bring back the divergence this task removes. Add a case in test_audit_task for a tracked `.claude/audit.config.json` edited during the attempt, so the behaviour is pinned either way. If the owner wants a tracked config edit refused, change the table row or the shared function once so both readers follow.

findings.issue: The comment says the scan is 'on what the readers MAY NOT NAME rather than on the instance that was found', and the task asked for the invariant, not the instance. What sc-ua5 does is a name blacklist: plugin_owned_under, PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE, attempt_strays and logs_dir. A reader that hardcodes `.claude/audit-backups`, keeps its own `under_any` list, or imports the table under another alias passes it (an `ImportFrom` alias is not a Name node). sc-ua6 only counts calls to `undeclared_changes`. It does not stop a reader from filtering the result again with a skip list of its own. The comment and docstring promise more than the check delivers.
findings.resolution: Either state the limit in the comment ('names the three primitives that were found; a differently spelled skip list is not seen') or widen the check to something the readers share. For example, assert that each reader has no local `skip`/`bookkeeping` list beyond its documented bookkeeping argument, and that it does not call `status_paths` or `under_any` itself.

findings.issue: The tree-wide scan passes on `outside == []` without counting the files it read. If the `os.walk(_output.SCRIPTS_DIR)` found no `.py` (a wrong anchor, or a skipped directory), the check would read as 'nobody else reads plugin_owned_under' and stay green. That is a filter narrowing to nothing, the shape the repo's no-silent-pass rule names. sc-ua7 shows the per-source scan can fail, but not that this walk reaches files.
findings.resolution: Collect the scanned names and assert the walk reached the home modules (`_manifest_io.py` and `_scoped_commit.py` among the files read) and more than a handful of files. Put the count in the check text so a narrowed walk goes red.

intent.note: Clause 'one function in _scoped_commit ... with the plan's bookkeeping, the plugin's run state and every PLUGIN_OWNED_IN_CLAUDE row taken out and returned separately as named plugin-owned state': undeclared_changes (_scoped_commit.py:1143-1184) takes the reader's bookkeeping plus run_state_rels out, splits `covered` from `strays`, splits every plugin-owned row into `pluginOwned`, and attributes the rest by snapshot, else mtime. Clause 'commit-task-work's attempt refusal, audit-task's _uncommitted_leftovers and drive-phase's set-aside call it, deleting their own skip lists': the commit and the close each call undeclared_changes once and the three local helpers and _run_state_rels are deleted. drive-phase deletes its own table walk and calls the shared plugin_owned_rels and split_plugin_owned. It does not call undeclared_changes itself, because the set-aside works from the commit's JSON answer (undeclared_split), which already comes from that function. That is a narrower reading of 'call it' but it holds the invariant, since the table and its placement have one home, and xs6 pins the result. Clause 'the close then never refuses a path the commit step left out': the close prints a plugin-owned line and no longer counts those paths. Declared paths are matched in `covered` before the plugin-owned split, so a task that declares a plugin-owned file is still held to committing it. Clause 'a case per reader ... a restore point appears during the attempt': lo-po1 to lo-po3 cover the close (accept, refuse-twin, no-files task). ctw-at7/at8 cover the commit and xs6 covers the set-aside; the executor says so, and none of those files was edited. Clause 'a lint or case that fails when a reader computes the skip list itself': sc-ua5 to sc-ua8, a name scan (see findings 2 and 3). The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately: the _uncommitted_leftovers arity change from 3 to 4, the new close output line, the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE edits and the drive-phase edit made under P137.1 although the brief lists P137.2 as its last declarer. attempt_strays has no remaining user outside the scan's own tuple (grep of plugins, tests, tools and the docs).
intent.redFirstBasis: The executor's own word is could-not-prove, and its basis holds. The helper ran `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_task.py tests/test__scoped_commit.py` in a throwaway tree at HEAD and got exit 1 with sc-ua1 to sc-ua6 and sc-ua8 failing. But the run against the working tree's implementation did not show every task test passing (no tally matched), so the red was not shown to turn green. By reading, lo-po1 fails on HEAD, because the HEAD close skips only bookkeeping and run state, so a restore point made during the attempt lands in `during` and is refused. I did not watch it fail.
intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate is the literal `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_task.py tests/test__scoped_commit.py`, so those two files are the bound. I read the regions that exercise the moved behaviour, not the whole of either suite: the new lo-po and sc-ua cases, the neighbouring close and leftover cases around `_leftover_cases`, and the commit and set-aside pins that ride on the same function (ctw-at7/at8/at9 in test_commit_task_work.py and xs6 in test_drive_phase.py, which the gate does not select). I found no existing case in those regions that would still pass with the shared function's behaviour deleted. The one swallow-shaped check is the task's own sc-ua8 (finding 3).
